- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — increase downward drift or add volatility buffer.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is flat or rising, true outcome often dips — adjust for downward momentum if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- When multiple auctions occur in 30d window (especially CAP3/DE), model underreacts to supply shock — increase downward adjustment by 5–10% of supply net magnitude.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility — apply asymmetric correction: +10% for bullish, -15% for bearish sentiment windows.
